sanskrit: iti te taṃ naravyāghraṃ praśaṃsanto mahārathāḥ nidrayā samavākṣiptās tūṣṇīm āsan viśāṃ pate
english: Thus praising that tiger among men, the great car-warriors, overcome by sleep, fell silent, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: aśvapṛṣṭheṣu cāpy anye rathanīḍeṣu cāpare gajaskandhagatāś cānye śerate cāpare kṣitau
english: Some slept upon the backs of horses, others within the boxes of their chariots, others seated on the shoulders of elephants, and still others upon the bare ground.

sanskrit: sāyudhāḥ sagadāś caiva sakhaḍgāḥ saparaśvadhāḥ saprāsakavacāś cānye narāḥ suptāḥ pṛthak pṛthak
english: With their weapons, with their maces, with their swords and battle-axes, with their lances and armor, the men slept each apart from the other.

sanskrit: gajās te pannagābhogair hastair bhūreṇurūṣitaiḥ nidrāndhā vasudhāṃ cakrur ghrāṇaniḥśvāsaśītalām
english: Those elephants, blind with sleep, with their trunks coiling like serpents' bodies and dusted with the earth's powder, cooled the ground with the breath of their nostrils.

sanskrit: gajāḥ śuśubhire tatra niḥśvasanto mahītale viśīrṇā girayo yadvan niḥśvasadbhir mahoragaiḥ
english: The elephants, breathing upon the surface of the earth, shone there like sundered mountains breathed upon by great serpents.

sanskrit: samāṃ ca viṣamāṃ cakruḥ khurāgrair vikṣatāṃ mahīm hayāḥ kāñcanayoktrāś ca kesarālambibhir yugaiḥ suṣupus tatra rājendra yuktā vāheṣu sarvaśaḥ
english: The horses, with their golden harnesses, made the level ground uneven, gashing the earth with the points of their hooves; and there, O king of kings, with their yokes hung with garlands, they slept, still harnessed everywhere to their teams.

sanskrit: tat tathā nidrayā bhagnam avācam asvapad balam kuśalair iva vinyastaṃ paṭe citram ivādbhutam
english: That host, thus broken by sleep, slept speechless, like a wondrous picture laid out upon a canvas by skilled hands.

sanskrit: te kṣatriyāḥ kuṇḍalino yuvānaḥ; parasparaṃ sāyakavikṣatāṅgāḥ kumbheṣu līnāḥ suṣupur gajānāṃ; kuceṣu lagnā iva kāminīnām
english: Those young warriors, wearing earrings, their limbs gashed by one another's arrows, slept clinging to the temple-globes of the elephants, as though pressed against the breasts of their beloved women.

sanskrit: tataḥ kumudanāthena kāminīgaṇḍapāṇḍunā netrānandena candreṇa māhendrī dig alaṃkṛtā
english: Then the eastern quarter of Indra was adorned by the moon, the lord of the water-lilies, pale as the cheek of a lovely woman, the delight of the eyes.

sanskrit: tato muhūrtād bhagavān purastāc chaśalakṣaṇaḥ aruṇaṃ darśayām āsa grasañ jyotiḥprabhaṃ prabhuḥ
english: Then, after a little while, the blessed lord marked with the hare showed his reddish glow in the east, the radiant one swallowing up the brilliance of the stars.

sanskrit: aruṇasya tu tasyānu jātarūpasamaprabham raśmijālaṃ mahac candro mandaṃ mandam avāsṛjat
english: And following that reddish dawn, the moon, little by little, let fall a great net of rays bright as gold.

sanskrit: utsārayantaḥ prabhayā tamas te candraraśmayaḥ paryagacchañ śanaiḥ sarvā diśaḥ khaṃ ca kṣitiṃ tathā
english: Driving away the darkness with their splendor, those rays of the moon slowly spread over all the quarters, over the sky, and over the earth as well.

sanskrit: tato muhūrtād bhuvanaṃ jyotirbhūtam ivābhavat aprakhyam aprakāśaṃ ca jagāmāśu tamas tathā
english: Then in a moment the world became as though made of light, and the darkness, dim and unillumined, swiftly fled away.

sanskrit: pratiprakāśite loke divābhūte niśākare vicerur na viceruś ca rājan naktaṃcarās tataḥ
english: When the world was lit up again and the moon, lord of the night, had become as bright as day, then, O king, the creatures that roam by night roamed about—or roamed no more.

sanskrit: bodhyamānaṃ tu tat sainyaṃ rājaṃś candrasya raśmibhiḥ bubudhe śatapatrāṇāṃ vanaṃ mahad ivāmbhasi
english: That army, being awakened by the rays of the moon, O king, came awake like a great grove of lotuses upon the water.

sanskrit: yathā candrodayoddhūtaḥ kṣubhitaḥ sāgaro bhavet tathā candrodayoddhūtaḥ sa babhūva balārṇavaḥ
english: As the ocean, stirred up at the rising of the moon, would surge in agitation, so did that sea of armies surge, stirred up at the moon's rising.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ punar eva viśāṃ pate loke lokavināśāya paraṃ lokam abhīpsatām
english: Then once more the battle broke out, O lord of the people, for the destruction of the world among men who longed for the world beyond.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tato duryodhano droṇam abhigamyedam abravīt amarṣavaśam āpanno janayan harṣatejasī
english: Saṃjaya said: Then Duryodhana, approaching Droṇa, spoke these words, given over to wrath, kindling both joy and ardor.

sanskrit: na marṣaṇīyāḥ saṃgrāme viśramantaḥ śramānvitāḥ sapatnā glānamanaso labdhalakṣyā viśeṣataḥ
english: Enemies who in battle were resting, worn out with toil, dejected in spirit, and who had found their opening—these are above all not to be borne with.

sanskrit: tat tu marṣitam asmābhir bhavataḥ priyakāmyayā ta ete pariviśrāntāḥ pāṇḍavā balavattarāḥ
english: Yet this we endured, out of a wish to please you; and now these Pāṇḍavas, well rested, have grown the stronger.

sanskrit: sarvathā parihīnāḥ sma tejasā ca balena ca bhavatā pālyamānās te vivardhante punaḥ punaḥ
english: In every way we are fallen short, in vigor and in strength, while they, protected by you, wax greater again and again.

sanskrit: divyāny astrāṇi sarvāṇi brahmāstrādīni yāny api tāni sarvāṇi tiṣṭhanti bhavaty eva viśeṣataḥ
english: All the celestial weapons, the Brahmā-weapon and the rest—all of these abide above all in you alone.

sanskrit: na pāṇḍaveyā na vayaṃ nānye loke dhanurdharāḥ yudhyamānasya te tulyāḥ satyam etad bravīmi te
english: Neither the Pāṇḍavas, nor we, nor any other bowmen in the world are a match for you when you fight—this truth I tell you.

sanskrit: sasurāsuragandharvān imāṃl lokān dvijottama sarvāstravid bhavān hanyād divyair astrair na saṃśayaḥ
english: O best of the twice-born, knowing every weapon, you could slay these worlds with their gods, asuras, and gandharvas by your celestial arms—of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: sa bhavān marṣayaty enāṃs tvatto bhītān viśeṣataḥ śiṣyatvaṃ vā puraskṛtya mama vā mandabhāgyatām
english: Yet you bear with these men, who are above all afraid of you—whether you do so out of regard for their pupilship, or for my own ill fortune.

sanskrit: evam uddharṣito droṇaḥ kopitaś cātmajena te samanyur abravīd rājan duryodhanam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Thus stung and provoked by your son, O king, Droṇa, filled with anger, spoke these words to Duryodhana.

sanskrit: sthaviraḥ san paraṃ śaktyā ghaṭe duryodhanāhave ataḥ paraṃ mayā kāryaṃ kṣudraṃ vijayagṛddhinā anastravid ayaṃ sarvo hantavyo 'stravidā janaḥ
english: Old though I am, I strive with utmost power in battle, Duryodhana; and beyond this, greedy for victory, I must even stoop to a base deed—all these folk who know not weapons must be slain by me who knows them.

sanskrit: yad bhavān manyate cāpi śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubham tad vai kartāsmi kauravya vacanāt tava nānyathā
english: Whatever you judge, be it good or be it evil, that indeed I shall do, O Kaurava, at your word, and not otherwise.

sanskrit: nihatya sarvapāñcālān yuddhe kṛtvā parākramam vimokṣye kavacaṃ rājan satyenāyudham ālabhe
english: Having slain all the Pāñcālas and shown my valor in battle, I shall lay aside my armor, O king—by my truth I lay my hand upon my weapon and swear it.

sanskrit: manyase yac ca kaunteyam arjunaṃ śrāntam āhave tasya vīryaṃ mahābāho śṛṇu satyena kaurava
english: And as for your thinking that Arjuna the son of Kuntī is weary in battle—hear, O mighty-armed Kaurava, in truth, of his prowess.

sanskrit: taṃ na devā na gandharvā na yakṣā na ca rākṣasāḥ utsahante raṇe soḍhuṃ kupitaṃ savyasācinam
english: Neither the gods, nor the gandharvas, nor the yakṣas, nor the rākṣasas dare to withstand in battle Savyasācin when he is enraged.

sanskrit: khāṇḍave yena bhagavān pratyudyātaḥ sureśvaraḥ sāyakair vāritaś cāpi varṣamāṇo mahātmanā
english: By him at Khāṇḍava the blessed lord of the gods himself was withstood, and though he poured down rain, he was checked by that great-souled one with his arrows.

sanskrit: yakṣā nāgās tathā daityā ye cānye balagarvitāḥ nihatāḥ puruṣendreṇa tac cāpi viditaṃ tava
english: Yakṣas, nāgas, and daityas, and others puffed up with their strength, were slain by that lord among men—this too is known to you.

sanskrit: gandharvā ghoṣayātrāyāṃ citrasenādayo jitāḥ yūyaṃ tair hriyamāṇāś ca mokṣitā dṛḍhadhanvanā
english: In the cattle-expedition the gandharvas, Citrasena and the rest, were vanquished, and you yourselves, being carried off by them, were set free by that firm-bowed one.

sanskrit: nivātakavacāś cāpi devānāṃ śatravas tathā surair avadhyāḥ saṃgrāme tena vīreṇa nirjitāḥ
english: The Nivātakavacas, too, the foes of the gods, who could not be slain in battle by the celestials, were conquered by that hero.

sanskrit: dānavānāṃ sahasrāṇi hiraṇyapuravāsinām vijigye puruṣavyāghraḥ sa śakyo mānuṣaiḥ katham
english: Thousands of dānavas dwelling in Hiraṇyapura that tiger among men subdued—how then can he be withstood by mortal men?

sanskrit: pratyakṣaṃ caiva te sarvaṃ yathā balam idaṃ tava kṣapitaṃ pāṇḍuputreṇa ceṣṭatāṃ no viśāṃ pate
english: And it is before your very eyes that this whole host of yours has been wasted by the son of Pāṇḍu, while we strove on, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: taṃ tathābhipraśaṃsantam arjunaṃ kupitas tadā droṇaṃ tava suto rājan punar evedam abravīt
english: As Droṇa thus extolled Arjuna, your son, enraged, O king, spoke to him once more these words.

sanskrit: ahaṃ duḥśāsanaḥ karṇaḥ śakunir mātulaś ca me haniṣyāmo 'rjunaṃ saṃkhye dvaidhīkṛtyādya bhāratīm
english: I, Duḥśāsana, Karṇa, and Śakuni my maternal uncle shall slay Arjuna in battle this day, after dividing the Bhārata host in two.

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā bhāradvājo hasann iva anvavartata rājānaṃ svasti te 'stv iti cābravīt
english: Hearing that speech of his, the son of Bharadvāja, as though laughing, fell in with the king and said, "May it be well with you."

sanskrit: ko hi gāṇḍīvadhanvānaṃ jvalantam iva tejasā akṣayaṃ kṣapayet kaś cit kṣatriyaḥ kṣatriyarṣabham
english: For who—what warrior—could destroy the wielder of Gāṇḍīva, blazing as if with splendor, the inexhaustible one, that bull among warriors?

sanskrit: taṃ na vittapatir nendro na yamo na jaleśvaraḥ nāsuroragarakṣāṃsi kṣapayeyuḥ sahāyudham
english: Him neither the lord of wealth, nor Indra, nor Yama, nor the lord of the waters, nor asuras, serpents, and rākṣasas could destroy, weapons and all.

sanskrit: mūḍhās tv etāni bhāṣante yānīmāny āttha bhārata yuddhe hy arjunam āsādya svastimān ko vrajed gṛhān
english: Only fools speak such things as those you utter, O Bhārata; for having met Arjuna in battle, who could return home unscathed?

sanskrit: tvaṃ tu sarvātiśaṅkitvān niṣṭhuraḥ pāpaniścayaḥ śreyasas tvaddhite yuktāṃs tat tad vaktum ihecchasi
english: But you, suspicious of everyone, harsh, fixed upon evil, would have those devoted to your welfare speak now this thing and now that.

sanskrit: gaccha tvam api kaunteyam ātmārthebhyo hi māciram tvam apy āśaṃsase yoddhuṃ kulajaḥ kṣatriyo hy asi
english: Go yourself, then, against the son of Kuntī—delay not, for your own sake; you too hope to fight, for you are nobly born and a warrior.

sanskrit: imān kiṃ pārthivān sarvān ghātayiṣyasy anāgasaḥ tvam asya mūlaṃ vairasya tasmād āsādayārjunam
english: Why will you have all these kings, who are guiltless, slain? You are the root of this enmity—therefore go yourself against Arjuna.

sanskrit: eṣa te mātulaḥ prājñaḥ kṣatradharmam anuvrataḥ dūrdyūtadevī gāndhāriḥ prayātv arjunam āhave
english: Here is your wise maternal uncle, the son of Gāndhāra, devoted to the warrior's duty—that gambler of crooked dice—let him march against Arjuna in battle.

sanskrit: eṣo 'kṣakuśalo jihmo dyūtakṛt kitavaḥ śaṭhaḥ devitā nikṛtiprajño yudhi jeṣyati pāṇḍavān
english: This man, skilled at dice, crooked, a gamester, a cheat, a deceiver, a player versed in trickery, shall conquer the Pāṇḍavas in battle!

sanskrit: tvayā kathitam atyantaṃ karṇena saha hṛṣṭavat asakṛc chūnyavan mohād dhṛtarāṣṭrasya śṛṇvataḥ
english: Endlessly have you and Karṇa boasted in your glee, again and again, vainly and out of folly, in the very hearing of Dhṛtarāṣṭra:

sanskrit: ahaṃ ca tāta karṇaś ca bhrātā duḥśāsanaś ca me pāṇḍuputrān haniṣyāmaḥ sahitāḥ samare trayaḥ
english: "I, dear son, and Karṇa, and my brother Duḥśāsana—we three together shall slay the sons of Pāṇḍu in battle."

sanskrit: iti te katthamānasya śrutaṃ saṃsadi saṃsadi anutiṣṭha pratijñāṃ tāṃ satyavāg bhava taiḥ saha
english: Such boasting of yours has been heard in assembly after assembly—now make good that vow, and prove yourself a man of his word along with them.

sanskrit: eṣa te pāṇḍavaḥ śatrur aviṣahyo 'grataḥ sthitaḥ kṣatradharmam avekṣasva ślāghyas tava vadho jayāt
english: Here stands before you the Pāṇḍava, your foe, not to be withstood—look to the warrior's duty; more praiseworthy for you is death than such a victory.

sanskrit: dattaṃ bhuktam adhītaṃ ca prāptam aiśvaryam īpsitam kṛtakṛtyo 'nṛṇaś cāsi mā bhair yudhyasva pāṇḍavam
english: Gifts you have given, pleasures enjoyed, scriptures studied, and the lordship you longed for attained; your task is fulfilled and you are free of debt—fear not, fight the Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: ity uktvā samare droṇo nyavartata yataḥ pare dvaidhīkṛtya tataḥ senāṃ yuddhaṃ samabhavat tadā
english: Having spoken thus, Droṇa turned in battle toward where the foes were, and then, the army being divided in two, the fight began once more.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tribhāgamātraśeṣāyāṃ rātryāṃ yuddham avartata kurūṇāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca saṃhṛṣṭānāṃ viśāṃ pate
english: Saṃjaya said: When but a third part of the night remained, the battle raged on between the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas, both filled with eager joy, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: atha candraprabhāṃ muṣṇann ādityasya puraḥsaraḥ aruṇo 'bhyudayāṃ cakre tāmrīkurvann ivāmbaram
english: Then Aruṇa, the forerunner of the sun, stealing away the splendor of the moon, brought on the dawn, making the heavens as if coppery red.

sanskrit: tato dvaidhīkṛte sainye droṇaḥ somakapāṇḍavān abhyadravat sapāñcālān duryodhanapurogamaḥ
english: Then, the army being divided in two, Droṇa, with Duryodhana at his head, charged against the Somakas, the Pāṇḍavas, and the Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: dvaidhībhūtān kurūn dṛṣṭvā mādhavo 'rjunam abravīt sapatnān savyataḥ kurmi savyasācinn imān kurūn
english: Seeing the Kurus split in two, Mādhava said to Arjuna: "These foes, these Kurus, let me bring round to your left, O Savyasācin."

sanskrit: sa mādhavam anujñāya kuruṣveti dhanaṃjayaḥ droṇakarṇau maheṣvāsau savyataḥ paryavartata
english: Granting Mādhava leave with the word "Do so," Dhanaṃjaya wheeled round, keeping the two great archers Droṇa and Karṇa to his left.

sanskrit: abhiprāyaṃ tu kṛṣṇasya jñātvā parapuraṃjayaḥ ājiśīrṣagataṃ dṛṣṭvā bhīmasenaṃ samāsadat
english: But the conqueror of hostile cities, learning Kṛṣṇa's intent and seeing Bhīmasena posted at the forefront of the fray, drew near to him.

sanskrit: bhīma uvāca arjunārjuna bībhatso śṛṇu me tattvato vacaḥ yadarthaṃ kṣatriyā sūte tasya kālo 'yam āgataḥ
english: Bhīma said: Arjuna, Arjuna, Bībhatsu, hear my words truly: the hour has come for which a warrior-woman bears a son.

sanskrit: asmiṃś ced āgate kāle śreyo na pratipatsyase asaṃbhāvitarūpaḥ sann ānṛśaṃsyaṃ kariṣyasi
english: If, now that this hour has come, you do not seize the better course, then, your worth set at naught, you will be playing the part of a coward in disguise of mercy.

sanskrit: satyaśrīdharmayaśasāṃ vīryeṇānṛṇyam āpnuhi bhindhy anīkaṃ yudhāṃ śreṣṭha savyasācinn imān kuru
english: By your valor pay off your debt to truth, to fortune, to duty, and to fame; break through the line, O best of fighters—make an end of these, O Savyasācin.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca sa savyasācī bhīmena coditaḥ keśavena ca karṇadroṇāv atikramya samantāt paryavārayat
english: Saṃjaya said: That Savyasācin, urged on by Bhīma and by Keśava, passed beyond Karṇa and Droṇa and beset the foe on every side.

sanskrit: tam ājiśīrṣam āyāntaṃ dahantaṃ kṣatriyarṣabhān parākrāntaṃ parākramya yatantaḥ kṣatriyarṣabhāḥ nāśaknuvan vārayituṃ vardhamānam ivānalam
english: As he came on at the forefront of the fray, consuming those bulls among warriors, the bulls among warriors strove with all their might against him, yet could not check him, growing as he was like a kindled fire.

sanskrit: atha duryodhanaḥ karṇaḥ śakuniś cāpi saubalaḥ abhyavarṣañ śaravrātaiḥ kuntīputraṃ dhanaṃjayam
english: Then Duryodhana, Karṇa, and Śakuni the son of Subala rained down floods of arrows upon Dhanaṃjaya, the son of Kuntī.

sanskrit: teṣām astrāṇi sarveṣām uttamāstravidāṃ varaḥ kadarthīkṛtya rājendra śaravarṣair avākirat
english: Setting at naught the weapons of all of them, that foremost of those who know the highest weapons, O king of kings, overwhelmed them with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: astrair astrāṇi saṃvārya laghuhasto dhanaṃjayaḥ sarvān avidhyan niśitair daśabhir daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Warding off weapons with weapons, the light-handed Dhanaṃjaya pierced each of them with ten sharpened arrows apiece.

sanskrit: uddhūtā rajaso vṛṣṭiḥ śaravṛṣṭis tathaiva ca tamaś ca ghoraṃ śabdaś ca tadā samabhavan mahān
english: A storm of dust was raised up, and likewise a storm of arrows, and a fearful darkness, and a mighty din arose at that time.

sanskrit: na dyaur na bhūmir na diśaḥ prājñāyanta tathā gate sainyena rajasā mūḍhaṃ sarvam andham ivābhavat
english: Neither sky nor earth nor the quarters could be discerned, things having come to such a pass; bewildered by the dust raised by the army, all became as if blind.

sanskrit: naiva te na vayaṃ rājan prajñāsiṣma parasparam uddeśena hi tena sma samayudhyanta pārthivāḥ
english: Neither they nor we, O king, could make out one another; only by guesswork did the kings keep up the fight.

sanskrit: virathā rathino rājan samāsādya parasparam keṣeśu samasajjanta kavaceṣu bhujeṣu ca
english: Car-warriors bereft of their chariots, O king, closing with one another, grappled by the hair, by the armor, and by the arms.

sanskrit: hatāśvā hatasūtāś ca niśceṣṭā rathinas tadā jīvanta iva tatra sma vyadṛśyanta bhayārditāḥ
english: Car-warriors whose horses and charioteers were slain, motionless and stricken with fear, appeared there then as though scarcely alive.

sanskrit: hatān gajān samāśliṣya parvatān iva vājinaḥ gatasattvā vyadṛśyanta tathaiva saha sādibhiḥ
english: The horses, clinging to slain elephants that lay like mountains, appeared lifeless, and so too did their riders along with them.

sanskrit: tatas tv abhyavasṛtyaiva saṃgrāmād uttarāṃ diśam atiṣṭhad āhave droṇo vidhūma iva pāvakaḥ
english: Then, withdrawing from the combat to the northern quarter, Droṇa stood in the battle like a smokeless fire.

sanskrit: tam ājiśīrṣād ekāntam apakrāntaṃ niśāmya tu samakampanta sainyāni pāṇḍavānāṃ viśāṃ pate
english: But seeing him drawn off apart from the forefront of the fray, the armies of the Pāṇḍavas trembled, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: bhrājamānaṃ śriyā yuktaṃ jvalantam iva tejasā droṇaṃ dṛṣṭvārayas tresuś celur mamluś ca māriṣa
english: Beholding Droṇa, resplendent and graced with glory, blazing as if with splendor, the foes shook, wavered, and grew faint, O sire.

sanskrit: āhvayantaṃ parānīkaṃ prabhinnam iva vāraṇam nainaṃ śaśaṃsire jetuṃ dānavā vāsavaṃ yathā
english: As he challenged the enemy host like an elephant in must, they did not reckon they could conquer him, even as the dānavas could not hope to conquer Vāsava.

sanskrit: ke cid āsan nirutsāhāḥ ke cit kruddhā manasvinaḥ vismitāś cābhavan ke cit ke cid āsann amarṣitāḥ
english: Some were robbed of all spirit, some of the high-minded were filled with wrath, some became amazed, and some were seized with indignation.

sanskrit: hastair hastāgram apare pratyapiṃṣan narādhipāḥ apare daśanair oṣṭhān adaśan krodhamūrchitāḥ
english: Some of the kings ground their finger-tips against their hands, while others, swooning with anger, bit their lips with their teeth.
